message: 60M. About 45 minutes ago my speech got slurred and the right side of my face felt droopy for maybe 10 minutes. It's back to normal now so I figured it was nothing, but wanted to check.

basis.quote: About 45 minutes ago my speech got slurred and the right side of my face felt droopy for maybe 10 minutes
basis.interpretation: New onset focal neurological deficits (slurred speech and right facial droop) consistent with possible acute stroke; sudden onset 45 minutes ago; transient resolution does not exclude active cerebrovascular event

output.reason: New sudden focal neurological deficits (speech and facial) warrant immediate emergency evaluation regardless of transient nature; stroke protocol requires urgent imaging and assessment.
output.patientMessage: Call 911 immediately. You experienced sudden speech difficulty and facial weakness that could indicate stroke. Even though symptoms improved, this requires emergency assessment right now. Do not drive yourself; ambulance transport is necessary.

notice.directive: Call 911 now. Do not drive yourself or wait for a message reply.

queries: transient facial droop slurred speech resolution
acute focal neurologic deficit TIA stroke

findings.quote: the right side of my face felt droopy

findings.finding: Time from symptom onset to presentation approximately 45 minutes

question.text: During those 10 minutes when your speech was slurred and face felt droopy, did you notice any weakness or numbness on the right side of your body, or any difficulty understanding what others said?
question.why: Facial droop and slurred speech with complete resolution raises concern for TIA. Presence or absence of additional motor or sensory deficits and comprehension changes would affect urgency and imaging needs.
question.quote: slurred speech and right facial droop

queries: transient facial droop slurred speech resolution
acute focal neurologic deficit TIA stroke

output.reason: 60-year-old with sudden slurred speech and right facial droop 45 minutes ago lasting ~10 minutes, now resolved — a transient focal neurologic deficit consistent with TIA, which carries high early stroke risk and requires immediate emergency evaluation despite resolution.
output.patientMessage: Please call 911 now, or get to an emergency department immediately — do not drive yourself. Brief slurred speech with facial droop that resolves can still be a warning of stroke, and the risk of a stroke is highest in the first hours to days, so urgent assessment and imaging are needed today even though you feel normal. If symptoms return while waiting, tell the dispatcher right away.
differential: Transient ischemic attack with high early stroke risk
Minor ischemic stroke with clinical resolution (imaging may still show infarct)
Other focal deficit mimic, e.g. metabolic cause such as hypoglycemia
